## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Service worker generated by the Next.js build

The application SHALL generate its service worker from src/app/sw.ts during next build via a prerendered route handler, with no separate build step or watcher process.

#### Scenario: Single-step production build emits the worker

- **WHEN** the production build runs (next build with no chained service-worker command)
- **THEN** the build output contains the prerendered service worker for the /serwist/sw.js path, with content-type application/javascript and service-worker-allowed "/" headers baked into the route metadata

#### Scenario: Dev serves the worker without a second process

- **WHEN** the dev server is started with next dev only
- **THEN** requesting /serwist/sw.js returns a compiled service worker, and editing src/app/sw.ts is reflected on the next request without restarting any process

### Requirement: Root-scope registration from the new worker URL

The client SHALL register the service worker from /serwist/sw.js with scope "/", relying on the served Service-Worker-Allowed header to widen the scope beyond the worker's path.

#### Scenario: Fresh client registers and controls the app

- **WHEN** a browser without a prior registration loads the app while online
- **THEN** the service worker at /serwist/sw.js is registered, installs, and (via skipWaiting and clientsClaim) takes control without requiring a second navigation

#### Scenario: Existing client migrates from the old URL

- **WHEN** a client still controlled by the worker previously registered at /sw.js loads the app while online
- **THEN** the page registers /serwist/sw.js and the new worker replaces the old registration through the standard update flow, with no user action required

### Requirement: Install-time precache covers static assets only

The service worker SHALL precache the build's static assets (build chunks and public assets) at install time, and SHALL rely on runtime caching for navigation documents.

#### Scenario: Static assets available offline after install

- **WHEN** the service worker has installed and activated on a fresh client
- **THEN** build chunks and public assets resolve from the precache while offline, even for pages never visited

#### Scenario: Navigation shells cached on first visit

- **WHEN** a page is visited while online after the worker controls the client
- **THEN** its navigation document enters the runtime PAGES cache and the page shell is reachable offline afterwards, while a never-visited page remains unavailable offline

### Requirement: Runtime caching semantics preserved across the integration swap

The worker SHALL apply the same runtime caching strategy table as before the migration (Serwist defaultCache) including the auth-route exclusion.

#### Scenario: Auth routes bypass caching

- **WHEN** any request under /api/auth/ is made
- **THEN** the worker forwards it to the network without reading or writing any cache

#### Scenario: API reads fall back to cache offline

- **WHEN** a same-origin GET request under /api/ previously succeeded online and the client is now offline
- **THEN** the cached response from the apis runtime cache is served, subject to its expiration policy
